# `m.options.contracts`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Reference data on options contracts: type, exercise style, expiration, and strike.

```python
m.options.contracts(symbols=None, *, underlying=None, contract_type=None, as_of=None, expired=False, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

| Methods | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Symbol` |
| `sort` | `ticker`, `underlying_ticker`, `expiration_date`, `strike_price` |
| `filters` | `expiration_date`, `expiration_date_gt`, `expiration_date_gte`, `expiration_date_lt`, `expiration_date_lte`, `strike_price`, `strike_price_gt`, `strike_price_gte`, `strike_price_lt`, `strike_price_lte` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Option contracts to describe; leave it out to list contracts. `dm.ALL` is refused. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and each one you delete stops being read. `last_by()`, `fetch()`, `history()`, and most polls also drop a deleted symbol's rows. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; by default, a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `underlying` | Only contracts of this exact Massive ticker, such as `"AAPL"` or `"I:SPX"`. A table of them in a `Symbol` column is read value by value, each as if passed alone. A live table is followed. In a static table, one failed value fails the call. |  |
| `contract_type` | `dm.ContractType.CALL` or `PUT`; leave it out for both. |  |
| `as_of` | The day whose contracts to list; leave it out for today. | The day to read the data as it stood on, as text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`. Leave it out for today's state. How far back you can go depends on your plan; this page's plan table says how much history each plan holds. |
| `expired` | True lists only expired contracts; False, the default, those still trading. |  |
| `sort` | `"ticker"`, `"underlying_ticker"`, `"expiration_date"`, or `"strike_price"`. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | The direction of `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows in total without `symbols`. With them, it counts per contract, so it has no effect. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | `strike_price`, `expiration_date`, and their range forms. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `ticker`: "The ticker for the option contract." | REST |
| `OptionRoot` | String | The OCC option root, read from `Symbol`: the symbol without its `O:` prefix and its last 15 characters (expiry, type, and strike), such as `SPXW` for `O:SPXW251219C06000000`. It is never mapped to the underlying: an adjusted contract keeps its own root, such as `AAPL1`. | REST |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST |
| `AdditionalUnderlyings` | String | If an option contract has additional underlyings or deliverables associated with it, they will appear here. See here (https://www.optionseducation.org/referencelibrary/faq/splits-mergers-spinoffs-bankruptcies) for some examples of what might cause a contract to have additional underlyings. The column holds Massive's value as JSON text. | REST |
| `Cfi` | String | The 6 letter CFI code of the contract (defined in ISO 10962 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_10962)) | REST |
| `ContractType` | String | The type of contract. Can be "put", "call", or in some rare cases, "other". | REST |
| `Correction` | long | The correction number for this option contract. | REST |
| `ExerciseStyle` | String | The exercise style of this contract. See this link (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Option_style) for more details on exercise styles. | REST |
| `ExpirationDate` | String | The contract's expiration date in YYYY-MM-DD format. | REST |
| `PrimaryExchange` | String | The MIC code of the primary exchange that this contract is listed on. | REST |
| `SharesPerContract` | double | The number of shares per contract for this contract. | REST |
| `StrikePrice` | double | The strike price of the option contract. | REST |
| `Underlying` | String | The instrument Massive links the row to, in the library's canonical symbol form; for an option, the linked instrument, not what the contract delivers. From REST `underlying_ticker`: "The underlying ticker that the option contract relates to." | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
